messages:
mina: Heads up — HorizonPay asked for a dedicated batching/queue config tweak. They saw a noticeable p95 latency regression after last week's kernel roll and are hitting queue timeouts in bursts.

mina: Quick summary of profiling (attached logs sent to s3): median latency 48ms -> 55ms (+15%), p95 210ms -> 360ms (+71%). Throughput per-GPU steady but queue wait time spiked. KV cache hit-rate for their typical workload: 72% (was ~85%).

samir: Do we know if kernel selection is falling back to non-optimized kernels?

mina: Yes — from the perf trace it looks like when sequence length > 512 we hit a kernel path that doesn't have our fused multihead attention, so per-token cost jumps. Also see more KV cache churn because HorizonPay's requests have lots of short prefix variations (small templated prompts with customer id in the prompt).

lara: So two contributing factors: kernel fallback on long tails + lower KV cache hit-rate causing more KV lookups and memory pressure.

mina: Exactly. For Dedicated we can tune batching heuristics (batch formation window and max tokens-per-batch), and impose a per-customer queue ceiling so they don't consume excessive token-batch slots during bursts. Proposed conservative targets below.

mina: Proposal (HorizonPay, dedicated pool gpud-ld-6):
```
{
  "queue_policy": "windowed",
  "window_ms": 15,
  "max_tokens_per_batch": 4096,
  "per_customer_token_cap": 200000,  // tokens/sec equivalent budget
  "max_queued_requests": 120,
  "kv_prefetch": true,
  "kv_prefetch_ttl_ms": 30000
}
```

samir: Why 15ms window? That seems smaller than other customers.

mina: We picked 15ms because their arrival distribution is very spiky at small inter-arrival times; larger windows pushed many sequences into the long-kernel path. Smaller window + token cap prevents runaway batch sizes on the long tail and keeps latency SLOs for short requests. Our offline sim shows p95 back to ~220ms with 15ms window and cap of 4096 tokens/batch.

lara: How confident are we wrt throughput loss? Any regression for other customers on same pool?

mina: Simulated throughput drop ~4% under steady load, but tail behavior improves. With per-customer token cap we protect other tenants — they saw their latencies reduced in the sim.

ops: We'll need a canary rollout and a circuit-breaker. If queue wait > 500ms for 30s, auto rollback. Also need to ensure autoscale still handles sustained demand.

mina: Agreed. Suggested rollout plan: apply config to one dedicated slab (gpud-ld-6a) for 1 hour, monitor p95/requests-queued/kv-hit, then expand to full pool. Canary CLI: `redwoodctl dedicated apply-config --pool gpud-ld-6a --customer horizonpay --file horizonpay-batch.json`

samir: Add a kernel-tagging tweak? If we force prefer-quantized-kernel for sequences <=512 we might avoid fallback for many of their requests. Any risk to quality?

mina: There is some quality delta for extreme corner cases but HorizonPay doesn't use generation-critical sampling in those tails. I'll coordinate with model-onboarding to add a canary kernel preference for this customer.

lara: Also add a short-lived KV cache warming step during rollout: prefetch common prefixes (we have a list of top-500 prompt prefixes for HorizonPay). That should improve cache hit-rate during the first minutes after rollout.

mina: I'll upload the prefix list to the canary config and enable kv_prefetch=true with TTL 30s as above.

engbot: deploy-bot: Canary config applied to gpud-ld-6a at 2026-03-16T11:02:15Z (job id cdr-2026-0316-11).

ops: Monitoring hooks requested: per-customer queued_requests, per-customer token_consumption, kernel_fallback_rate, kv_hit_rate. Hook them to the HorizonPay canary dashboard.

mina: I'll create a dashboard and share the link.

samir: One more ask — expose a soft token budget that returns 429 when exceeded (instead of letting requests queue indefinitely). That helps clients degrade gracefully.

mina: Good call. We'll set `soft_budget_action=\"reject\"` when per_customer_token_cap exceeded and toggle it after 1 hour if stable.

lara: LGTM. Make sure the rollout notes include a quick rollback command: `redwoodctl dedicated rollback --pool gpud-ld-6a --job cdr-2026-0316-11`

mina: I'll create the PR with the horizonpay-batch.json, the canary runbook, and the dashboard. Will ping here when PR is ready. :thumbsup:

ops: Thanks — keep us posted.

mina: PR posted: https://redwood.internal/p/horizonpay-dedicated-batch-config (includes perf traces and sim data).

samir: :eyes: Reviewing the sim artifacts now.

lara: If canary looks good, let's schedule overnight full-pool rollout to minimize user impact.

mina: Sounds good.
